decisions.assessment: The effective edits constrain well-formed producer output (direct /Extensions, nonempty/non-null /Kids and positive /Count, indirect /StructTreeRoot, reserved encryption permission bits). They do not by themselves require a reader to reject legacy or malformed forms. For #475, adjacent Table 24 prose explicitly says processors ignore all flags outside named positions. Existing targeted tests provide evidence for select paths; do not infer exhaustive support from them.
decisions.reconsideration: No owner-policy change proposed. Preserve reader recovery policy as separately scoped.

decisions.assessment: #13 Text annotations point at the ImageMask, Alternates, SMask, StructParent, ID and OPI entries and add an informative cross-reference to §11.6.5.2; treat as a note directing readers to existing restrictions. #211 is an informative NOTE 1 adjacent to §7.6.2’s signature-Contents encryption exception and clarifies its relation to signature representation in §7.9.2.4/Table 255. It does not add a new mandatory parser rejection rule. #475 adds the reserved permission-bit row in the errata appendix; the operative Table 24 prose tells processors to ignore flags outside the listed positions.

Issue #251 replaces the sentence that says an absent timezone has GMT relation with equivalent wording (+0'00), and separately strikes the sentence saying the remaining date fields are specified in local time. Existing `date.rs` notes the first is semantically equivalent; the date grammar supports field interpretation after the second is removed. The implementation stores fields and derives UTC instants. This does not settle calendar validity of all numeric date combinations.
decisions.reconsideration: No separate date-policy ADR change proposed.

decisions.assessment: §7.3.9 physical48/printed33 contains undefined-reference-as-null and null-dictionary-value-as-omission. §7.3.10 physical49/printed34 repeats undefined-reference-as-null and direct/indirect equivalence; it does not contain the dictionary omission rule.
